extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: A dataset for open book question answering, modeled after open book exams for assessing human understanding of a subject. It consists of 5957 multiple-choice questions and 1326 elementary-level science facts. The questions require combining a core science fact with broader common knowledge to answer novel situations.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.citeAs: Mihaylov, T., Clark, P., Khot, T., & Sabharwal, A. (2018). Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering. arXiv preprint arXiv:1809.02789.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created using a multi-stage crowdsourcing process. Given a set of core science facts (F), crowd workers were asked to think of a second common fact (k) that could be combined with a core fact to derive a new valid assertion. This assertion was then converted into a question-answer pair and extended into a 4-way multiple-choice question. The process included automatic filtering to ensure hardness for retrieval and association-based systems, crowd filtering to ensure answerability by a layperson, and expert filtering to ensure higher quality in Dev and Test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The crowdsourced second facts (K) were often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to the question, indicating potential missingness or noise in the additional facts provided.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The core facts (F) were derived from a subset of the WorldTree corpus, which was analyzed for sufficiency for elementary-level science. The additional facts (K) were crowdsourced from workers who marked a second fact needed for each question.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent multiple stages of filtering: automatic filtering to ensure hardness for retrieval and association-based systems, crowd filtering to ensure answerability by a layperson, and expert filtering to ensure higher quality in Dev and Test sets. Questions were also checked for uniformity of answer choices and absence of negation words to avoid trivial solutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers were asked to generate questions based on core science facts and mark a second fact needed for each question. The questions were then verified for hardness and answerability by additional crowd workers and experts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The dataset includes an analysis of the additional common knowledge needed to answer questions, categorizing the facts into types such as ISA, PROPERTY, DEFINITION, CAUSAL, and BASIC. The analysis showed that most questions require simple facts that should be easily retrievable from any knowledge base or textual corpora.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code for the models are available at http://data.allenai.org/OpenBookQA. The dataset includes Train, Dev, and Test splits, with the Dev and Test sets further filtered by in-house experts to ensure higher quality.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to probe a deeper understanding of both the topic and the language it is expressed in, requiring multi-hop reasoning and combining core facts with common knowledge. This has implications for assessing human-like reasoning in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases introduced by human annotators during the crowdsourcing process, as evidenced by the performance of simple neural baselines that highlight inevitable human bias in any crowdsourced dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset requires multi-hop reasoning and combining core facts with common knowledge, which is challenging for state-of-the-art QA methods. The additional facts (K) provided are noisy and may not always be directly relevant to the question. The dataset also has limitations in terms of domain specificity, as it focuses on elementary-level science questions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-Tuning for open book question answering systems. The dataset is designed to evaluate the ability of systems to combine core facts with broader common knowledge and perform multi-hop reasoning.
